description: Cross-service wire contract for the JOB FIRE PATH: the headers the BFF puts on POST /v1/internal/skills/submit and the ones the Python worker tier requires to be there. ADR-0046's Risks section records why this file exists: the route guard read `x-internal-token` while every caller in the repo sent the token under its old, product-prefixed name, so every scheduled run 403'd in a real deployment — and nothing caught it, because the two sides are tested separately and each test pinned its own spelling. Two tests that agree with themselves prove nothing about a boundary. TS: `apps/workspace/tests/lib/jobs/fire-headers.test.ts` submits a real run through `submitAgentRun`'s builders and asserts the headers that actually go out cover every name below. Python: `packages/agent/tests/test_fire_path_contract.py` asserts each set the backend requires is a SUBSET of the names below, read off the modules themselves (`routes/internal_auth._TOKEN_HEADERS`, `context_envelope._INTERNAL_TOKEN_HEADER_NAMES`, `jobs/runner.WORKER_IDENTITY_HEADERS`, `project_context.REQUEST_CONTEXT_ENVELOPE_HEADER`). Either side moving a name alone fails one of the two. Every name here is lower-case; HTTP header names are case-insensitive and both tests compare case-insensitively, but the file states one spelling so a diff never turns on casing. The twin at `apps/workspace/tests/fixtures/job_fire_headers.json` is byte-identical, for the reason `request_context.json` gives: the frontend typecheck/test Docker build context is scoped to `apps/workspace` and cannot COPY a file from outside it.
sentByBffComment: Everything a fully-populated fire carries: `content-type` and the service token from `lib/jobs/backend-client.ts::submitJob`, the rest from `buildRequestContextWireHeaders` in `lib/jobs/service.ts::submitAgentRun`. Values are omitted rather than sent empty when the corresponding lookup returns nothing (an org with no model overrides sends no `x-model-overrides`), so this is the CEILING of what goes out, and `requiredOnEveryFire` below is the floor. `x-disabled-sources` is deliberately absent: the fire path passes no `disabledSources` — a job's sources are its own column.
requiredOnEveryFireComment: What the ROUTE refuses without. `routes/internal_auth._require_internal_token` is the whole gate on this path: no session, no JWT, one shared secret. This is the exact set whose spelling broke every scheduled run once.
internalTokenAcceptedSpellingsComment: The guard and the envelope middleware both accept the old name too, and the BFF sends the new one. The old name is not spelled here: `test_fire_path_contract.py` derives it from this one with `legacy_name`, the way `LegacyHeaderNamesMiddleware` does, until the contract step (`agent_host.legacy_headers`).
contextEnvelopeComment: The signed envelope (backlog T3-9). `context_envelope.RequestContextEnvelopeMiddleware` enforces it on this path for WorkOS-authenticated callers and EXEMPTS internal-token service calls — so the fire path is not refused without it. The BFF sends it anyway, and this contract keeps it that way: it is what the worker reads the run's tenancy out of when the individual headers are eventually dropped, and an exemption is a bad thing to discover you were relying on. The signature header is omitted when `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` is unset (dev), which is why it is listed here and not in `requiredOnEveryFire`.
workerIdentityHeadersComment: The names the BFF sends. `jobs/runner.WORKER_IDENTITY_HEADERS` holds them under their old names, the ones the backend readers read until the contract step; `test_fire_path_contract.py` derives those with `legacy_name`, as `agent_host.legacy_headers` copies them. `jobs/runner.WORKER_IDENTITY_HEADERS` — the headers the worker SYNTHESISES onto the tool context from the run's identity, so a project-scoped tool inside an unattended run reads the same names a chat turn does. They are here because they must be spelled identically to what the BFF sends on the wire: `remember` answered 'no project in scope' on every deep-research run when they were absent, and it would answer the same on a rename that only one side made.
